subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stout Warcraft-style dwarf smith with a huge braided red beard and horned iron helm. He stands behind a stump-mounted anvil with a raised hammer in his right fist and tongs holding a glowing ingot in his left.
spec.layout: Scale: the dwarf is 1.5 m to the helm top (horn tips 1.6 m), standing at x=0, z≈0 and facing +Z toward the anvil. Warcraft proportions: oversized head (~0.3 m wide with helm), massive pauldrons, thick forearms, fist-sized hands and big boots on short legs. His feet are planted at x=±0.15 with toes forward. The torso is barrel-shaped: shoulders ±0.30 at y≈1.08, belly front surface at z≈0.26 around y 0.8, chest front at z≈0.20 at y 1.0, and the back at z≈-0.2. The huge braided beard hangs from the chin (y 1.28) down to y≈0.75 in front of the chest, its front reaching z≈0.38. Below it a blue-trimmed leather apron covers the belly and thighs to y 0.30. Arms are bent forward in an A-pose: upper arms angle down and out from the shoulders to elbows at (±0.51,0.84,0), and forearms point almost straight forward to wrists at (±0.52,0.73,0.31), so both hands reach out toward the anvil. The right (-X) fist grips a warhammer-style smithing hammer, held raised diagonally up-forward with its head hovering about 10 cm above the anvil face. The left (+X) fist holds long tongs angled forward and slightly up, gripping a glowing orange ingot that lies on the anvil face. The anvil (long axis along X, face centred at z=0.68, top y=0.80, horn pointing to the dwarf's left +X) stands on a chunky tree-stump (y 0 to 0.38) with iron hoops. A few embers float above the ingot. Style: Blizzard/Warcraft. Chunky, exaggerated, faceted low-poly shapes (6-8 sided cylinders, boxes with bevelled edges). Every metal edge has a bronze or gold trim part, with rivets and studs as separate small parts. Colour contrast is warm (red-orange hair, ruddy skin, bronze and gold) against cool steel and Ironforge blue cloth. The ingot, embers and the eyes' small catch-lights are the only glowing/bright parts (use the glow kit on ingot, embers and ingot-lit rivets).

parts.builds: Pelvis and short, thick legs, with the skeleton chains hipL/kneeL/ankleL/toeL and the same on R. Legs are wide tapered sweeps in clothDark trousers with leather knee pads (leatherLight, studded with bronze). Big chunky boots in leather with ironDark toe caps, iron-shod soles (a thin ironDark slab under each boot), bronze buckles and a folded cuff at y≈0.30. The belt is a thick leatherDark band round the hips at y 0.70 with a big gold buckle plate (a square with a bronze centre boss), small bronze studs, a small pouch (leather), a hung spare hammer and a ring of keys or tools (iron). The lower leather apron skirt (leather body, leatherDark stitching strips, bronze rivets along the edges, a blue clothBlue hem stripe) hangs from the belt to y≈0.30 in front (front surface z≈0.28), and a darker back flap. The apron has scorch marks as small ink-coloured patches. Boots are 0.26 long (heel z≈-0.07, toe z≈0.26) and 0.14 wide, resting on y=0.
parts.attaches: The hips/hipL/hipR joints are at hipsCenter; the belt sits at beltLine, where the upperBody torso's bottom meets it. The apron bib (upperBody) overlaps the apron's top edge at y≈0.72. Boots sit at footL and footR on y=0.

parts.builds: Barrel torso (a loft/sweep over hips-spine-chest, 0.30 half-width at the shoulders, belly bulging to z≈0.26 at y 0.8, from y 0.62 to 1.22), a thick short neck (skin) from neckBase, and a clothBlue sleeveless tunic/jerkin with a darker clothDark trim at the collar and around the arm holes. Over it goes a leather chest harness: crossed leatherDark straps with iron buckles, a leather apron bib (leather, with a bronze rivet border and a small gold anvil emblem) from y 1.05 down to the belt at z≈0.26. Huge Warcraft pauldrons on pauldronL/R: layered domed iron plates (ironDark, with iron plates and ironLight rim edges), each with a bronze trim ring and three bronze spikes or studs, plus a short leather strap. A leather-wrapped tool roll or small backpack (leather, leatherDark straps) on the back at z≈-0.28. A gold-rimmed iron gorget ring at the neck base is optional.
parts.attaches: The bottom meets the belt at beltLine; the neck top meets the head part at neckBase/headCenter below the beard. Pauldrons wrap the shoulderL/R joints at pauldronL/R. The arms part's upper arms begin inside the pauldrons at shoulderL/R. The beard (head part) hangs in front of the bib and covers it down to y≈0.75.

parts.builds: The head is the hero feature. The skull is a broad box-like shape with a heavy brow, at headCenter (about 0.30 wide, 0.30 high), in ruddy skin. The face is built first: two small deep-set eyes (eyeWhite with eyeBlue iris and ink pupil, with a tiny white catch-light) under thick beardDark bushy brow ridges that slope in an angry scowl. A big round bulbous nose in noseRed with a skinShade underside and two nostril dots, plus cheekbones and rosy cheeks. Pointed ears out the sides. A separate lower jaw on the jaw joint, with a heavy chin and lower teeth (teeth), and an upper lip with two upper teeth under the moustache so the mouth can open. The upper head rides head. Nothing sits in front of the face except the moustache. The iron helm sits on top: a ironDark half-dome cap with an iron brow band, bronze trim rim, gold rivets, a nose-free open face, a short central ridge or crest (iron), and two curved ironLight/bone-coloured horns (teeth colour) sweeping out and up from the sides, with bronze bases. The huge beard has a solid beard-coloured mass from the cheeks and chin down to y≈0.75 and out to z≈0.38, with layered overlapping blade-like locks in beard, beardLight (tips) and beardDark (roots/underside). On it hang two thick braids on each side of the centre, bound with gold rings and bronze clasps, ending in tassel points. A sweeping moustache in beard with curled braided ends at the cheeks. Sideburns blend into the beard and from under the helm back to a short ponytail behind the head (beard colours, with a gold tie).
parts.attaches: The head base sits on the neck top at neckBase (y≈1.2) with the joints head and jaw. The beard root begins at beardRoot and chinPoint and hangs over the upperBody bib and chest, staying within z≤0.38. The ponytail hangs behind at z≈-0.2.

parts.builds: Both bare muscular arms, built as chains (shoulderL/elbowL/wristL with fingersL/thumbL and the same on R) with sweeps for skin that bend at the joints. The upper arms are thick (radius ≈0.075 at the shoulder, bulging biceps), the forearms thicker still (≈0.075-0.085), with a ring of short beardDark arm hair tufts. Each forearm wears a leather bracer (a sleeve of leather with leatherDark straps, bronze studs and a bronze/gold buckle) from just before the wrist to mid-forearm. Left wrist: a thin gold band. The hands are big blocky fists in skin: a palm block, four chunky finger segments on each hand curled to grip (the right fist wraps the hammer handle at gripHammer along hammerDir; the left fist wraps the tongs handle at gripTongs, aimed along the direction toward tongsTip), plus a thumb on thumbL/thumbR. Knuckle bumps and skinShade fingernails or creases; a soot-dark ink smudge patch on the forearms.
parts.attaches: Upper arms begin inside the pauldrons at shoulderL/R (upperBody); elbows are at elbowL/R and wrists at wristL/R. The right fist closes around the hammer handle at gripHammer; the left fist closes around the tongs at gripTongs (both are built by the props part and the fists build to the same mounts).

parts.builds: The smith's hand tools, static (no joints). The warhammer: a woodDark/wood handle (octagonal) running from a pommel at gripHammer - 0.12 along hammerDir up to hammerHead (0.62 long total), with leatherDark grip wrap bands at the fist and a leather wrist strap loop. Its head is a heavy iron block (0.26 long across, 0.13 high, 0.13 deep) at hammerHead with its long axis roughly along world X and perpendicular to the handle. It has an ironLight bright striking face on the +X end and a pein (tapered wedge) at the other end, bronze collar bands where the handle enters, and gold rivets. The tongs: two long iron arms (ironDark, with ironLight highlight edges) crossing at a bronze rivet pivot, with leather-wrapped handles at gripTongs and flat gripping jaws at tongsTip. They are 0.5 long from gripTongs to tongsTip, along the direction (tongsTip - gripTongs). The glowing hot ingot is a flat rectangular bar (0.20 long × 0.05 wide × 0.04 thick, centred at ingotCenter along ingotAxis, resting on the anvil face) made from fireOrange body with a fireHot core strip, and an ember-red dark end where the jaws grip it. The ingot and its small bright elements use the glow kit (strength 1.2-1.6). About 10 spark and ember particles are small diamond/sphere parts (fireHot and fireOrange) floating around 0.82-1.15 m above the anvil near the ingot (x 0.0-0.45, z 0.65-0.9), each glowing, some elongated like streaks.
parts.attaches: The hammer handle passes through the right fist at gripHammer, its head hovering above the anvilTop face (~10 cm gap). The tongs run from the left fist at gripTongs to the ingot at ingotCenter, with the jaws at tongsTip. The ingot rests on the anvil face at anvilTop (y=0.80).

parts.builds: A heavy blacksmith's anvil on a tree stump, all static. The stump is a chunky 8-sided wood cylinder (wood body with woodDark bark ridges and vertical grooves, radius 0.30, from y=0 to 0.38, centred at stumpCenter) with root flares at the base and a pale top ring pattern (woodDark growth rings and a lighter wood centre inside the top). Two iron hoops (ironDark with ironLight edges, and rivets) wrap the stump at y≈0.08 and 0.30, and there are axe-nick wedge cuts. On it is the anvil, long axis along X: a wide flat foot base (ironDark, 0.5 long × 0.28 deep, y 0.38-0.46), a tapered waist (ironDark) and the face plate on top (iron slab, top at y=0.80, spanning x -0.42 to 0.42, z 0.53 to 0.83), with an ironLight polished top surface strip and bright edges. A long conical horn (iron with an ironDark underside) points to the dwarf's left (+X), curving gently up to a tip at x≈0.68. On the heel (-X side) there is a stepped cutting table, a square hardy hole and a round pritchel hole in ink colour on the face top. Bronze or gold decorative trim bands run along the waist, with a small gold rune or Ironforge emblem on the side facing the viewer (+Z), plus dents and scorch spots (ink) on the top face and an iron chain or pouch hanging from the stump (optional).
parts.attaches: The anvil top face is at the anvilTop mount (y 0.80, z 0.68) for the hammer, tongs and hot ingot to rest above it. The stump rests on y=0, centred at stumpCenter (z=0.68), in front of the dwarf's boots (which reach z≈0.26).

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith figure with a skeleton rig, around 1.4m tall and broad-built with a large beard, positioned facing an anvil with a hammer gripped in the right hand.

I'm thinking through the pose: arms in a slight A-pose angled forward, with a hammer held vertically in the right hand and tongs gripping a glowing ingot in the left, positioned over the anvil. I'm breaking the model into parts—torso/legs with spine and leg joints, head with beard and face details, arms with pauldrons and gear, and the anvil with its stand.

For the anvil setup, I'm keeping it simple with an anvil on a tree stump, a glowing ingot, and sparks, skipping extra forge details like a water bucket. I'm settling on five parts total—body, head/beard, arms/hands, props (hammer, tongs, ingot, sparks), and anvil/stump—budgeting roughly 170 units each for a total under 900, and now working out the dwarf's overall height including a possibly horned helmet.

Now I'm laying out the exact vertical coordinates for hips, shoulders, neck, head, and helm top, along with the horizontal extents for shoulders and arms, plus placing the anvil and hammer within the overall bounding box. I'm starting to define the skeleton's joint hierarchy beginning with the hips as the root.

Still placing leg joints...

Bending the arms slightly forward with wrists around (0.60,0.66,0.22) and (-0.62,0.66,0.22), adding simple hand joints with thumb and finger digits per side, left holding tongs and right holding a hammer grip point at the wrist.

I'm angling the hammer head forward-up at roughly 45°, computing its position by extending along the grip direction, and checking placement against the anvil (stump 0–0.42, anvil top around 0.85-0.88) to make sure there's no collision while positioning it near the strike surface.

I'm adjusting the horn to point at +x 0.62 to avoid clashing with the tongs, and reconsidering the anvil's distance from the dwarf's belly so the arms can actually reach it. I'm also rethinking the hammer position—rather than holding it far from the anvil, I want the head positioned near or over the anvil to look like it's about to strike.

Checking the hammer head position confirms it hovers about 10cm above the anvil face, a good mid-swing pose. Now for the left hand tongs, I'm positioning the wrist and angling the tongs forward so the gripped tip rests down on the anvil surface near y 0.84.

I'll settle on mount points: ingot center around [0.22,0.83,0.78], tong tip at [0.28,0.83,0.72], and grip at the wrist [0.50,0.72,0.30], checking the length and direction vector work out consistently. Then I'm mirroring the setup for the hammer grip on the right side with the shoulder position adjusted accordingly.

The wrists end up slightly asymmetric, which is fine for a natural stance, with the hammer gripped in the right fist pointing upward. I'm proportioning the torso with a protruding belly and chunky Warcraft-style pauldrons at the shoulders, then positioning the anvil and hammer head so the strike point lines up correctly.

Now I'm working out the overall bounding box, checking the horn, pauldrons, and hammer head extents to settle on a centered size of roughly 1.4 by 1.6 by 1.3.

I'm settling on a size of [1.4, 1.58, 1.15] with z spanning from the dwarf's back around -0.25 to the anvil front near 0.9, and placing the head joint and head center to size up the oversized dwarf head with forward-facing features.

Now I'm designing the massive braided beard hanging from the chin down to around y=0.75, with metal rings, a big red nose, and heavy brow ridges with small blue eyes. I'm settling on an iron-and-bronze half-dome helmet with brass trim and short curved horns, paired with a red-orange Bronzebeard-style braided beard, making sure the beard box doesn't collide with the anvil or overlap awkwardly with the head and chest geometry.

Now I'm laying out the torso box spanning the chest and shoulders, and the leg box beneath it, planning how the body part combines legs, torso, and the hanging beard into one coherent figure.

I'm reorganizing into cleaner groupings: lower body covering hips, legs, boots, belt, and apron with their joints; upper body for torso, chest armor, pauldrons, backpack, and neck; a separate head group with beard and helm; and arms as their own group with hands and bracers.

Adding forge props (hammer, tongs, ingot, sparks) and an anvil/stump as the remaining two parts, keeping to six total with a budget split around 130/140/190/140/110/120. Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy starting from hips as root, up through spine and chest, with positions and directions for each.

Continuing the chain, I'm placing neck, head, and jaw joints with specific pivot coordinates, working out the jaw hinge position relative to the head center so the face sits forward correctly. Then I start on the leg joints, beginning with the left hip position.

Now moving to arms: shoulderL off chest aiming down-out, elbowL positioned and oriented toward the wrist, wristL extending further out and down. I'm working out the joint chain coordinates to keep proportions natural for the arm.

Still placing joints, finishing the right arm and hammer grip point, then setting hip and leg heights before moving to the color palette for the dwarf's skin, beard, and other details.

Finalizing the palette at exactly 24 colors, covering skin, beard, iron, bronze, gold, leather, cloth, teeth, fire, and wood tones, with the anvil using the iron shades and the stump built from the wood colors.

Now I'm working out the mount points for the rig -- hips, belt, neck, head, chin, beard root, shoulders, elbows, wrists, grip points for the hammer and tongs, and the anvil's top position.

Adjusting ingot center to y=0.822 so it rests just above the anvil top, with tongs tip matching at 0.82. For the hammer, I'm computing the head center from the grip position plus half the handle direction, placing it around (-0.39,0.985,0.76), then working out the head's long axis perpendicular to the handle.

Now positioning the pommel at the back of the handle around (-0.57,0.715,0.26), and planning small glowing sparks floating above the anvil near the strike point. I'm setting the anvil geometry with its stump centered at (0,0,0.68) and a bounding box roughly spanning from (-0.46,0,0.38) to (0.72,0.80,0.98).

I'm refining the anvil's shape -- waist, face plate, horn pointing toward +x, hardy and pritchel holes, and a stepped heel at -x -- giving it an x range from about -0.42 to 0.68 with a box of [-0.42,0,0.38] to [0.68,0.82,0.98]. I'm also considering adding scorch marks, scale fragments, and iron hoop bands on the stump for extra detail, with the stump resting flush on the floor at y=0.

Now I'm placing the props: an ingot sitting on the anvil, a hammer with its head extending along x from -0.52 to -0.26, y 0.9-1.07, z 0.70-0.82, and a pommel near (-0.57, 0.715, 0.26), all enclosed in a box roughly [-0.62,0.68,0.2] to [0.58,1.12,0.9]. I'm also tracing the tongs from the grip point (0.5,0.72,0.34) to the tip (0.28,0.82,0.72), making sure the bounding box overlaps correctly with the gripping hand.

Moving to the arms, I'm defining the upper arm box spanning from shoulder down through the hands, considering leather bracers and bare brawny forearms fitting a dwarf blacksmith look rather than sleeves, with pauldrons mounted separately in the upper body and the arm tube feeding into them. I'm also sizing the upper body box to accommodate the pauldrons properly.

Now I'm working on the lower body — a basic box plus a leather apron extending from chest to knee, belt tools, and a small hammer at the hip, trying to decide whether the apron bib should be owned by the upper or lower body group.

I'm placing the apron skirt in the lower body between y 0.28-0.70, and the bib portion in the upper body from y 0.72 to 1.05 with a neck strap, making sure the beard overlaps correctly in front of the bib without clipping. I'm nailing down the front z-depths for the torso: chest around 0.20, belly around 0.26, with the beard sitting further forward at 0.30 so it layers naturally in front of the bib.

Then I set the head's bounding box, mark only the lower body and anvil as floor-contacting (for boots and base), and lay out the budget allocation across body parts -- lower 140, upper 150, head 200, arms 120, props 110.

Now I'm drafting the part specs for a chunky Warcraft-style dwarf: massive head, huge shoulders, thick forearms, oversized boots and hands, flat two-tone colors with bronze trim and rivets. I'm detailing the stance -- feet planted apart facing the anvil, short wide legs, iron-shod boots with a bronze buckle and cuffed top. Then I'm starting the joints hierarchy JSON with groups for legs, arms, and head, ordering parent-child relationships from hips through spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, and hip joints.

I'm continuing the joint chain down each leg (knee, ankle, toe) and arm (shoulder, elbow, wrist, fingers, thumb), making sure each joint's parent is the preceding one in its chain and names stay alphanumeric without underscores. I'm also figuring out whether the head should split into an upper head piece and a separate jaw piece, with the beard riding on the head and a moustache tuft possibly attached near the jaw.

I'll have the beard mass and moustache attach to the head rather than the jaw, keeping the jaw as a simple lower box with chin and teeth that peeks out from the beard. For the mouth, I want it visible beneath the moustache as a dark slot with small teeth so the face reads as a scowling grin rather than being fully hidden. Now I just need to finalize the joint directions and write it all out, making sure the JSON stays valid and the mount values line up correctly.
